chat._note: Current client values, served so they can change without a release. context_window_fallback_tokens is the first one to tune: 32000 is wrong for most models we route to today, and it silently caps how much fits in project chat. Image sizing is NOT here on purpose: it is already served per tier at tiers.feature_definitions.images, and a second source for the same field is how the free-tier copy drifted.

retry._note: Retry schedule and copy for a chat turn whose connection dropped. auto_delays_ms is the ladder of AUTOMATIC attempts after the failure; when it is exhausted the client stops and waits for a manual tap. The countdown is honest because we own the timer, unlike a progress bar for a finish we cannot predict. Delays are milliseconds so the ladder can be tuned without a release.

redeem._note: Served copy for an offer-code redemption that did not visibly succeed. Today the client shows NOTHING on failure, and it presents nothing until this block is served: no English fallback on a subscription surface. THREE outcomes, chosen by the client from what it observed. promo_redeem_unconfirmed: no transaction ever arrived, so we genuinely cannot say why, and the copy must not pretend otherwise. promo_redeem_settling: a transaction arrived and verify_failure is 'failed' or ABSENT; nothing for the user to do. promo_redeem_settling_signed_out: a transaction arrived with verify_failure = 'deferred_no_token'; signing in applies it. ABSENT verify_failure MUST pick plain settling: 'we never learned a reason' is not 'we know you are signed out'. redeem_timeout_ms is accumulated FOREGROUND milliseconds after returning from the App Store, not wall clock from the tap, because the App Store hop is when iOS reclaims the process. secondary_action is a GP-owned allowlist: 'retry_redeem' or absent. No contact_support (there is no destination) and no sign_in in v1 (needs client work; the text carries it instead). No time estimate anywhere on purpose: we do not know how long settling takes, and a number nobody measured is the honest-progress rule broken.
